**HTTP mode**, for clients that connect to MCP servers by URL, like ChatGPT (Developer Mode).

```bash
hma-mcp --http --rom-dir "C:/hacks"
cloudflared tunnel --url http://127.0.0.1:3333
```

The server prints a URL with a secret token (`.../mcp/<token>`). Give your client the same path on the tunnel's address. Setup details are in the [README](https://github.com/dewayneku/hma-mcp#quick-start), under "ChatGPT and other clients that connect by URL".

- **Secret token:** requests without it get "not found". A new one is made each run; `--token` or `HMA_MCP_TOKEN` keeps one.
- **One folder:** `--rom-dir` is the only folder the server may read ROMs and images from or save to. It also works in normal (stdio) mode.
- **Local only:** the server listens on 127.0.0.1, so the tunnel is the only way in.

Also: the server now reports its real version (it had been stuck at 0.1.0), and "save as" must be a `.gba` file.

HTTP mode was tested with the included HTTP test client on Windows, Linux and macOS, but not yet with ChatGPT itself. Reports are welcome.

### Download

| You use | Get |
|---|---|
| Claude Desktop | `hma-mcp-win32.mcpb`, `hma-mcp-darwin.mcpb` (Apple Silicon) or `hma-mcp-linux.mcpb`, then double-click it |
| ChatGPT, Claude Code, other clients | `hma-mcp-<system>.zip` / `.tar.gz`; unpack it, then run `hma-mcp --http` for URL-based clients, or point your client at `hma-mcp` |

The builds are self-contained, so you don't need .NET. On macOS, run `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine <folder>` on a downloaded build before starting it.
